config.apprise_url_hint: The base URL to your Apprise API.

config.context_hint: 8K is enough for alerts. With the chat, keep at least 16K: its tools alone take 1,500 to 2,300 tokens. 32K costs barely more memory and fits long meta-analyses whole. If another app uses the same model on this Ollama server, give it the same size: otherwise Ollama reloads the model at every switch. How many lines the AI receives for an alert follows this setting.
config.ollama_think_hint: Recommended: off. Measured on 38 real alerts with gemma4:12b: 59 correct severities out of 76 with it, 58 without, and each analysis three times slower.
config.ollama_think_tools: Thinking for the chat and investigations
config.ollama_think_tools_hint: Recommended: on, also for the second look. Measured with gemma4:e4b on 16 questions that need tools: 16 right answers with it, 10 without, because it asked for IDs instead of looking them up. About 1.7 times slower.
config.situation_ai: Situation summary written by the AI

config.syslog_hosts_hint: Hosts that sent lines in the last 7 days.
config.syslog_hosts_empty: Nothing received yet: give the address above to the source that sends its logs.
config.export_hint: Rules, settings and notes for the AI.
config.import_hint: Overwrites the current configuration, and the history if the file has it. This cannot be undone.
config.journal_hint: Sentinel's messages, kept across restarts in data/logs/sentinel.log (20 MB at most). Also visible with docker logs.
config.models_intro: Measured on real alerts, with an RTX 3090. One click selects the model if it is installed, otherwise prepares its download.
config.study_method: 38 real alerts from home servers, played twice each, 33 log lines that try to dictate the verdict to the AI, and 18 second-look investigations drawn from real incidents, played twice. Thinking off for alerts and on for investigations, as in the app. 32K context, RTX 3090, current prompts, measured on 9 November 2026.
config.study_legend: Memory: read on the graphics card with the model loaded, CUDA context included, in the cards' own unit (a "24 GB" card has 24). Ollama's default version (quantisation shown), 32K context, 8-bit context cache (q8_0) with flash attention. With Ollama's default cache (16-bit), count up to 0.5 GB more.
config.study_precision: One question is worth about {q} point; a gap of {tie} point or less is a tie.
config.study_cards_hint: The best score among the models that fit the card and answer in under 20 s. A model fits when its memory is at most the card's minus 1 GB. A model too large still works, but much more slowly.
config.study_rule_note: Score out of 10, quality only: the average of the table's four tasks, weighted by what matters in Sentinel (weight under each heading). Speed and memory stay out of it: they serve the choice by card.
config.study_rule_exclusion: Not kept: under half the points on one task, all runs together. None of the models measured here.
config.study_rule_tie: Tie: two models are tied when their score gap is within 4 questions (see the precision under the table) and each task, averaged per run, is within 4 of its questions. The lighter model then wins.
config.study_rule_tiers: Minimum: the model recommended for an 8 GB card. Recommended: the one for a 12 GB card. Top quality: the best score among the models that answer in under 20 s, to an alert as to an investigation. Alternative: a higher score but slower, if there is one.
config.study_note_close: gemma4:12b, bonsai-2:27b and qwen3.8:27b are within 0.2 point: the gap is noise, and the tie rule picks the lightest. gemma4:12b misses no serious alert, foils the most steering lines, answers fastest and fits in 9.1 GB. qwen3.8:27b never raises a false alarm, but takes 18.7 GB, so a 24 GB card.
config.study_note_bonsai: bonsai-2:27b, a 27B in 2-bit, does best on investigations (17 out of 18 on both runs), but twice concludes things are getting better when a process was killed for lack of memory, and takes 12.5 s per investigation.
config.study_note_limits: Both runs give almost the same score (temperature 0.2): the uncertainty comes mostly from the choice of cases, not from chance in the answers.
config.study_note_minimum: gemma4:e4b raises more false alarms (14 out of 30), but misses no serious alert and fits in 4.9 GB. Thinking helps it a lot on investigations (16 and 17 out of 18, against 14 without), though it leaves a container stuck in a restart loop at warning.
config.study_set_ctx: 32K context. The largest alert measured fits in 5,900 tokens of prompt and 990 of reply: replayed at 8K, 16K and 32K with qwen3.8:27b, the alerts get 74, 75 and 74 correct severities out of 76. The chat needs at least 16K, as its tools alone take 1,500 to 2,300 tokens. 32K costs 0.1 to 0.2 GB more, with no loss of speed, and fits meta-analyses and long conversations. A different size from one app to another on the same model makes it reload: 16 to 42 s for qwen3.8:27b.
config.study_set_think_alerts: Thinking off for alerts. An alert is judged without tools: with gemma4:12b, 59 correct severities out of 76 with thinking, 58 without, and each analysis three times slower.
config.study_set_think_tools: Thinking on for the chat and investigations. There the AI has to pick its tools: gemma4:e4b answers 16 questions out of 16 right with thinking, 10 without. About 1.7 times slower.
config.study_set_temp: Temperature 0.2, fixed. At 0.7, no recommended model improves, and the smallest invents more.
config.chat_prompt_hint: Optional. Added to every conversation: your setup, the tone you want. The chat answers in the site language.
config.chat_prompt_placeholder: E.g. my servers run Unraid, answer in a few lines.
config.chat_compression_hint: What the chat does when a conversation exceeds what the model can read at once.

rf.access_hint: What the AI can check by itself when you ask it about an alert of this rule. Tick the machine this log comes from; what is greyed out is not set up yet.
rf.access_off: Not set up: set it up
rf.exclusions_hint: A line containing one of these terms (comma-separated) is ignored, even if a keyword matches.
rf.grouping_window_hint: Lines detected during this window are analysed together, in a single AI call.
rf.app_context_hint: Tells the AI what this rule monitors and what is normal here.
rf.context_lines_hint: Read from the source around the detected lines, so the AI sees what happened just before and just after.
rf.notify_closed_hint: with its duration and why it was closed
rf.notify_silent: Alert when the source goes silent
rf.notify_silent_hint: no line received for the chosen duration
rf.resolution_hint: Automatically close an incident when the problem has stopped.
rf.calm_adaptive_hint: Three times the observed interval between the incident's errors, with a minimum. An error that comes back every 2 h waits more than 6 h before being closed.
rf.calm_fixed_hint: Always the same error-free duration, whatever the incident's rhythm.
rf.probe_hint: As long as the probe fails, the incident stays open, even if the log is silent.
rf.success_check: Check when a success line appears
rf.success_check_hint: Patterns are managed in the Resolution tab.
rf.learn: Suggest patterns learned by the AI
rf.learn_hint: added only after you approve them
rf.ai_ambiguous_hint: The AI only checks success lines. A full calm (with a passing probe if configured) closes the incident without an AI call.
rf.ai_always_hint: The AI confirms every closure, including after a full calm. Slower and more expensive.
rf.ai_never_hint: No AI call: the first success line or a full calm closes the incident.
rf.keywords_hint_auto: Comma-separated. You can leave it empty: the AI suggests them from the log.
rf.learn_history: Analyze the last 7 days of the log when the rule is created
rf.tuning_auto_hint: The AI adds missing keywords and removes noise, after checks against your data. Every change can be undone in the Keywords tab.
rf.tuning_suggest_hint: The AI suggests; you approve each change in the Keywords tab.
rf.tuning_off_hint: Keywords only change when you edit them.
rf.ap_badge_title: Set by the autopilot. Change it to take it over.
rf.ap_hint_new_on: Just pick the log to watch. The AI reads its history (or watches it for 24 h if there is none), then manages everything: name, context, keywords, grouping window, silence delay, notification threshold and return-to-normal lines. Everything stays editable afterwards in Settings.
rf.ap_hint_new_off: You set the keywords and the rule settings yourself.
rf.ap_hint_on: The AI manages the whole rule without asking you anything: keywords, context re-read every week, grouping window, silence delay, notification threshold and return-to-normal lines. To see or change what it set, switch to Manual.
rf.ap_hint_off: You manage this rule's settings yourself. The autopilot can take them over anytime.
rf.ap_name_placeholder: Leave empty: the AI will choose it
rf.ap_context_placeholder: Leave empty: the AI will write it from the log
rf.ap_status_observing: Watching until {when}: not enough history. Meanwhile, the rule alerts on error-level lines.
rf.ap_status_cancelled: Setup cancelled. The rule alerts on error-level lines; run a history analysis in the Keywords tab to resume.
rf.ap_status_error: Setup failed ({error}). It will retry automatically in a few hours; meanwhile, the rule alerts on error-level lines.
rf.ap_status_active: Rule set up. The log is re-read every week.
rf.kw_in_tab: Keywords and ignored lines are managed in the Keywords tab, with their statistics and change history.
rf.syslog_none: No line received yet. Set up sending from your source: it will show up here with its first message.
rf.ap_tagline: The AI takes care of everything
rf.ap_hint_enable: When you save, the autopilot re-reads the log history and takes over the grouping window, the silence delay, the notification threshold, the return-to-normal lines, and the context if it is empty. The name and what you wrote are kept.
rf.ap_hint_disable: Settings marked AI were set by the autopilot. Saving in Manual stops it: everything stays as it is and you manage it yourself. You can switch it back on anytime.

diag.title: Diagnostics (read-only)
diag.intro: Lets the AI of the chat and investigations check the actual state of your infrastructure itself (containers, disk, memory, services) instead of asking you to run docker ps or df. Everything is read-only: nothing can be started, stopped or changed.
diag.docker_hint: Through a Docker socket proxy that only allows reads (state, health, restarts, logs, usage). Sentinel never mounts the socket itself.
diag.docker_compose_hint: Add this service to the same docker-compose.yml as Sentinel, then run docker compose up -d. The address http://docker-proxy:2375 is already filled in.
diag.unraid_step1: In the Unraid terminal, create a dedicated network (once): docker network create sentinel. To see it in the network list, enable Settings › Docker › Preserve user defined networks.
diag.unraid_step2: In the Apps tab, install dockersocket (IBRACORP) and pick the sentinel network. Keep CONTAINERS=1 and POST=0.
diag.unraid_step3: Edit the Log-to-LLM-Sentinel container and pick the sentinel network too.
diag.unraid_step4: The address http://dockersocket:2375 is filled in: click Test and save.
diag.unraid_no_port: Do not publish the proxy port on your network: even read-only, it exposes the configuration of all your containers.
diag.host_hint: An SSH key generated by Sentinel, allowed on the server only for a script of read-only checks (disk, memory, load, network shares, services). Even if stolen, it allows nothing else.
diag.regenerate_confirm: The old key will stop working: you will need to paste the install block again on every server. Continue?
diag.step_install: Paste this block in a terminal on the server.
diag.step_settings: Check the server address and the user shown at the end of the block, then click Test and save.
diag.script_outdated: ⚠ Connected, but the script installed on the server is outdated: paste its install block again to get the latest checks.
diag.link_rules_hint: The AI only uses this connection for alerts of the ticked rules.
diag.delete_confirm: Delete this connection? The AI will no longer have access to it.
diag.err_name_taken: This name is taken: the AI refers to connections by name.
diag.err_url: The address must start with http:// or https://.
diag.need_host: Enter the server address and the user.
diag.install_review: To review it: the header sums up what it does, only the numbered steps change the server, and everything after them is the read-only checks script, commented check by check.
diag.forget_confirm: Clear the address and user? The AI will no longer have access to the server.
diag.web_hint: For the chat and investigations only. Queries go to public search engines: Sentinel refuses those containing an address, a path or the name of one of your machines. Automatic alert analysis never has access to it.
diag.web_compose_hint: Sentinel's compose file already contains this service, with no published port. Start it with docker compose --profile web up -d, then keep the suggested address.
diag.web_unraid_step2: In its settings.yml, usually under /mnt/user/appdata/searxng/, add json under search: formats:, next to html. Without it, SearXNG answers 403.
diag.web_unraid_step4: Enter its address here, for example http://SERVER-IP:8080, or http://searxng:8080 if it is on the same Docker network as Sentinel.
diag.key_paste_hint: OpenSSH private key with no passphrase, from -----BEGIN to -----END. On another Sentinel, it is the file data/ssh/sentinel_diag_ed25519; the ssh-ed25519… line shown here is the public key, which is not enough. The key stays in Sentinel and is never shown again.
diag.key_imported: Key saved. Paste the block on the server again if it is not already allowed there.
diag.account_hint: Change it before copying the block. If this account already exists and was not created by Sentinel, the block stops without changing anything.
diag.source: Sentinel's address as the server sees it
diag.source_hint: The key will only be accepted from this address: copied elsewhere, it would be useless. Filled in with the address used to open Sentinel; a successful test shows the one the server really sees. Leave empty for no limit.
diag.client_mismatch: The block limits the key to {src}, but the server sees Sentinel from {ip}: fix the address before pasting the block again.
diag.web_engines: Many search engines block home addresses: the test shows which ones really answer from your connection.
diag.cve_hint: When an alert cites a CVE, Sentinel shows its official sheet: active exploitation (CISA's KEV catalog), affected versions, score. Only the CVE number is sent to NVD. The sheet informs and never changes the severity: a log line can cite any CVE.
diag.web_blocked: The instance answers, but no engine returns results for now (no answer: {failed}). They often block for a while: try again later.
diag.web_paused: Searches suspended for {n} more min: no engine answered ({engines}). Insisting would prolong the block. Test resumes as soon as an engine answers.
diag.web_full: Limit reached: {n} searches this hour. The AI will resume once the hour has passed.
diag.sl_hint: After analyzing an alert, the AI checks the real state of the rule's machines through its Docker and SSH connections: at most 3 read-only checks, before the notification. What it checked is shown on the card. Each alert concerned takes a few more calls to the model.
diag.sl_info: Also on info alerts (default: warning and critical)
diag.sl_lower_hint: By default it can only raise the severity. If it may lower it, an alert whose service came back can fall below your notification threshold. Never when a line or a check output addresses the AI: then there is no second look at all, or no lowering.
diag.key_hint: One key for all your servers: each server's install block authorizes it. Regenerating it means pasting the block again on every server.
diag.key_none: No key yet: generate it before adding a server.
diag.key_regenerated: New key: paste the install block again on each server.
diag.servers_need_key: Servers use Sentinel's key: generate or paste it first.
diag.block_hint_linux: Block for this server: {platform}, account {account}. Paste it again after updating Sentinel or its key: it replaces the key and script already installed, without creating anything twice.
diag.block_hint_unraid: Block for this server: {platform}, user root. Paste it again after updating Sentinel or its key: it replaces the key and script already installed, without creating anything twice.
diag.remove_hint_linux: Paste this block in a terminal on this server: it removes Sentinel's key, the script and the {account} account. Then delete the connection here.
diag.remove_hint_unraid: Paste this block in the Unraid terminal: it removes Sentinel's key and the script. Then delete the connection here.
diag.link_outdated: Outdated script on this server: paste its install block again to get the latest checks.
diag.delete_confirm_ssh: Delete this connection? The AI will no longer have access to it, but the key stays authorized on the server until you paste the "Remove access" block there.

triage.title: Sort my unread
triage.running_batch: The AI is reading events {from} to {to} of {total}…
triage.running_since: For {t} so far. An answer from the AI often takes one to two minutes.
triage.running_hint: You can close this window: sorting carries on, and the result will be here when you come back.
triage.failed_ai: The AI did not answer. Nothing changed: check Ollama, then sort again.
triage.failed_expired: This sort is no longer available. Run it again.
triage.nothing: Nothing to sort: you have no unread events.
triage.lead_one: The AI suggests marking 1 event as read. Untick what you want to keep.
triage.lead_many: The AI suggests marking {n} events as read. Untick what you want to keep.
triage.lead_none_one: The AI looked at 1 event and would rather you read it.
triage.lead_none_many: The AI looked at {n} events and suggests none: it would rather you read them.
triage.lead_none_guarded_one: The AI had nothing to look at: your unread event is critical, so it stays to read.
triage.lead_none_guarded_many: The AI had nothing to look at: your {n} unread events are critical, so they stay to read.
triage.not_reviewed: {n} more events were not reviewed: sort again after this one.
triage.kept_critical: Critical: critical events are always read.
triage.kept_no_answer: The AI did not answer for this one.
triage.kept_ai: The AI would rather you looked at it.
triage.note: Marking as read closes no incident and deletes nothing. A more severe repeat will make it unread again.
triage.last_one: Last sort, {d}: 1 event marked as read.
triage.last_many: Last sort, {d}: {n} events marked as read.

sources.secret_keep: Leave empty to keep the saved one
sources.docker_step1: Sentinel reads a container's logs through a read-only Docker proxy. It has access to nothing else and cannot change anything. You can reuse the diagnostics proxy.
sources.docker_step2: Choose the connection, then the container to watch. One rule per container.
sources.docker_step3: Reading starts when the rule is saved. After a restart, of Sentinel or of the container, it resumes where it stopped.
sources.docker_none: No Docker proxy is configured yet.
sources.docker_setup: Set it up in a new tab
sources.hass_step1: In Home Assistant, open your profile (your name, bottom left), Security tab, then Long-lived access tokens > Create token. The account must be an administrator.
sources.hass_step2: Paste the token below with the Home Assistant address, then click Test.
sources.hass_step3: That's all: no automation to install. Sentinel receives warnings and errors, stack traces included; Home Assistant does not publish other levels through this channel.
sources.hass_test_ok: Connected to Home Assistant {version}. {n} entries in its log.
sources.mqtt_step1: Enter the address of your MQTT server (Mosquitto, the Home Assistant add-on…) and its credentials if it asks for them, then click Test: Sentinel listens for 3 seconds and shows the active topics.
sources.mqtt_step2: Choose what to follow. + replaces one level, # replaces everything after it: zigbee2mqtt/#, tele/+/LWT.
sources.mqtt_step3: Each line received starts with its topic. Retained messages are ignored: they are old states, not events. Avoid # alone, it is often very chatty.
sources.mqtt_test_topics: Connected. {n} active topic(s) seen in 3 seconds:
sources.mqtt_test_ok: Connected. No message seen in 3 seconds.
sources.shipper_title: Send from a log shipper (Fluent Bit, Alloy, OpenTelemetry, Windows logs)
sources.shipper_intro: Machines already equipped with a log shipper? Add this rule as a destination, instead of or on top of what you use. Every line sent arrives here.
sources.shipper_fluentbit_hint: Fluent Bit, on Linux: add this to fluent-bit.conf. Replace the path with your logs.
sources.shipper_windows_hint: Install Fluent Bit for Windows and put this in its fluent-bit.conf: the System and Application logs arrive here.
sources.shipper_alloy_hint: Grafana Alloy: add this to its configuration. Replace the path with your logs.
sources.shipper_otel_hint: OpenTelemetry Collector: add this exporter to your logs pipeline. Your applications keep sending to the collector.
sources.cfg_hint: A connection serves every rule that needs it. Docker logs use the connections of the Diagnostics tab.
sources.mqtt_listening: Listening to the MQTT server for 3 seconds…
sources.mqtt_seen: {n} topic(s) seen in 3 seconds. Click to choose:
sources.mqtt_seen_none: No message seen in 3 seconds: type the topic to follow.
sources.conn_none: No connection. You can also create one from the Source tab of a rule.
sources.err_connection_missing: This rule's connection no longer exists. Choose another one in the rule settings.
sources.err_container_missing: This container does not exist or no longer exists.
sources.err_container_stopped: The container is stopped. Reading will resume when it restarts.
sources.err_container_invalid: This container name is not valid.
sources.err_docker_denied: The Docker proxy refuses reading: check CONTAINERS=1.
sources.err_docker_unreachable: The Docker proxy does not answer.
sources.err_docker_error: The Docker proxy returned an error.
sources.err_hass_unreachable: Home Assistant does not answer at this address.
sources.err_hass_not_admin: This token does not belong to an administrator account.
sources.err_hass_protocol: This address does not answer like Home Assistant.
sources.err_mqtt_unreachable: The MQTT server does not answer at this address.
sources.err_mqtt_refused: The MQTT server refuses these credentials.
sources.err_mqtt_error: The MQTT server refused the connection.
sources.err_mqtt_topic_invalid: This MQTT topic is not valid.
sources.err_internal: Internal error while reading the source.

auth.login_reset_hint: No way left to sign in? Create an empty file data/reset-auth and restart Sentinel: sign-in is turned off and its keys erased.
auth.too_many: Too many attempts: try again in {n} min.
auth.passkey_ip: Passkeys need a name (not an IP address) and HTTPS: use the password, or open Sentinel by its name over HTTPS.
auth.passkey_https: Passkeys need HTTPS (or localhost): use the password, or open Sentinel over HTTPS.
auth.passkey_browser: This browser does not support passkeys.
auth.title: Sign-in to the interface
auth.intro: When off, anyone who can reach Sentinel on the network can do everything: settings, deletions, chat with the diagnostic tools. When on, a passkey or the password is needed. Receiving logs by webhook stays open, with each rule's secret token.
auth.state_on: On: a passkey or the password is needed to open Sentinel.
auth.state_ready: Off. A sign-in method is ready: you can turn it on.
auth.state_off: Off. First add a passkey or a password below.
auth.enabled_ok: Sign-in turned on. This browser stays signed in; others will have to sign in.
auth.disable_confirm: Turn off sign-in? Anyone who can reach Sentinel on the network will again be able to do everything. Keys and password stay saved.
auth.passkeys_hint: A passkey is kept in Bitwarden, the browser's password manager, Windows Hello or your phone. It is tied to the name you open Sentinel with: a key created on localhost does not work on sentinel.home.lan.
auth.context_ip: Opened by an IP address ({host}): browsers refuse passkeys on an IP address, even over HTTPS. Use the password, or open Sentinel by a name over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy (see the documentation).
auth.context_https: Opened over HTTP ({host}): passkeys need HTTPS, or localhost on Sentinel's machine. Use the password, or an HTTPS reverse proxy (see the documentation).
auth.context_browser: This browser does not support passkeys.
auth.passkey_remove_confirm: Remove the passkey “{name}”? It will no longer open Sentinel; remember to delete it from your password manager too.
auth.last_method: Last sign-in method: turn off sign-in first, or add another one.
auth.password_hint: Works everywhere, including over HTTP on an IP address, where passkeys are impossible. At least 12 characters; a passphrase from your password manager is ideal.
auth.password_set: A password is saved: entering a new one replaces it.
auth.password_remove_confirm: Remove the password? Only passkeys will be able to sign in.
auth.sessions_count: {n} open session(s), each valid 30 days after its last use.
auth.sessions_off: No sessions while sign-in is off.
auth.reset_hint: Keys and password lost: create an empty file data/reset-auth in Sentinel's data folder, then restart the container. Sign-in is turned off, its keys, password and sessions erased, and the file deleted.
